rubrics.justification: Provides a generally plausible blastocyst description of ICM and TE, but overstates certainty from a single image and introduces a grading-stage dispute with the provided Gardner 2AA label rather than cleanly interpreting the reported morphology.
Integrates age, BMI, tubal factor, ovarian response, endometrium, first-cycle status, and semen data into prognosis reasonably well, though some links are speculative and AMH is unavailable.

Overall logic is mostly coherent, but there are inconsistencies such as discussing multiple embryos/two-embryo transfer despite the case not presenting that choice, and some speculative claims about sperm motility and embryo competence.

Many recommendations are guideline-consistent (SET at age 33, hydrosalpinx caution, PGT-A not routine), but there are deviations such as suggesting all multiple untested embryos can be transferred and some imprecise Gardner staging commentary.

Gives practical next steps including SET, luteal support, prenatal vitamins, alcohol cessation, and hydrosalpinx evaluation, plus reasonable future-cycle considerations, though some advice remains generic.
